subject.title: [Feature]: Feature Request: Batch Tool Calls + Context Block Management + Plan Enforcement

question: Which, if any, of the three requested tracks should OpenClaw core own now versus plugins or ClawHub?
rationale: The request spans native tool schemas, context/session storage semantics, config flags, and runner enforcement policy, and repository guidance keeps optional orchestration out of core unless a missing seam is proven.

options.title: Split and sponsor missing core seams
options.body: Keep the umbrella open but drive separate design decisions for batching, context clearing/block APIs, and plan gating, adding core/plugin APIs only where existing hooks cannot support the workflow.

options.title: Route to plugins until a seam is proven
options.body: Document supported plugin/context-engine approaches and keep core work paused until a narrower issue demonstrates a missing API or contract.

options.title: Decline native orchestration now
options.body: Close or defer the umbrella as too broad for the current roadmap while leaving narrower concrete regressions or missing APIs to separate issues.

recommendation.title: Split and sponsor missing core seams
recommendation.body: Keep the umbrella open but drive separate design decisions for batching, context clearing/block APIs, and plan gating, adding core/plugin APIs only where existing hooks cannot support the workflow.

likelyOwner.reason: Most current-history signals cross the requested planning, tool parameter, and runner behavior surfaces.
